text:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency breach detected on route /v1/chat/stream (dedicated-east-2). p99 > 1.5s for last 5m, auto-paging to oncall. link: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/streams

Ava (oncall): Acked. I'm on it. What are the current p95/p99 numbers and which customers are impacted?

Jia (eng-sre): Grafana quick view: p95 jumped from ~120ms -> ~430ms; p99 from ~490ms -> ~2.1s in the last 6m. Streaming stall rate +230%. Cursor: streaming stall counter shows a spike that coincides with precision-profile rollout at 00:03UTC. https://grafana.redwood.example/d/streams?panelId=9

Sam (eng-runtime): Was there a precision profile change today? I see a rollout of "precision-profile:v3-int8-aggressive" at 00:01UTC by the deploy pipeline. Could be related.

Devin (ml-infra): Calibration job logs show repeated OOMs on 3 nodes during int8 calibration step. Pods in k8s: redwood-calib-* are CrashLoopBackOff. Quick check: `kubectl -n infra get pods | grep calib` -> shows the crash loops.

Sam (eng-runtime): That matches prior incidents where failed calibration left runtime in a de-optimized path and triggered expensive dequant ops. Recommend immediate rollback of the precision profile to last-known-good (v2-safe-quant). Rollback command (internal CLI):
```
redwoodctl rollout set-precision --pool dedicated-east-2 --profile v2-safe-quant --reason "rollback: p99 spike after v3-int8"
```
If we can't apply cluster-wide, can we toggle safe-fallback mode on the serving runtime? `SVC_FALLBACK=enabled` toggles conservative decode path.

Ava (oncall): I'm running the rollback now. Ping me when it's started. I'll open a short incident page and notify CS.

deploy-bot: precision-rollout service: starting rollback of precision-profile:v3-int8-aggressive -> v2-safe-quant for pool dedicated-east-2 (initiated by Ava). Request id: rld-2026-03-14-01

Jia (eng-sre): Observability notes: traces show a sharp increase in time spent in dequantize_kernel and memcpy between 00:02-00:06. Sample stack (from rts logs):
```
#0  0x7f6a3a1 dequantize_kernel
#1  0x7f6a3b2 decode_step
#2  0x7f6a3c3 continuous_batcher
memcpy bytes/sec spiking in the same window
```
Possible root cause: calibration emitted a profile that led to a slow codepath (fallback to software dequant) under certain sequence lengths.

Devin (ml-infra): Dump from calibration pod: `OOMKilled` and large allocations during stats collection. Looks like the calibration sample set included a few extremely long sequences (~65k tokens) which blew up memory usage due to naive histogram building. Need to add sequence-length cap in calib job.

Sam (eng-runtime): Good catch. For immediate mitigation besides rollback we should: 1) disable aggressive int8 conversion for streaming models, 2) enable kvcache-size guard, 3) add a runtime config to fallback to fp16 when dequant path exceeds latency threshold. I'll open PRs after the incident.

Maria (cs): Which customers saw visible impact? Support queue shows three enterprise customers (Acme, Voyager, Vireo) reported slow streaming or partial responses. I flagged them as P0. I'll prepare a short note once we have a confirmed rollback outcome.

Ava (oncall): Rollback completed as of 1923456865. deploy-bot shows: precision profile rollback finished for pool dedicated-east-2. Monitoring for 5m post-rollback.

deploy-bot: Rollback completed successfully. New active profile: v2-safe-quant.

Jia (eng-sre): Initial metrics post-rollback (1m window): p95 dropped back to ~130ms, p99 trending down to ~520ms. Streaming stalls reduced ~85% from peak. Keeping watch for residual tail.

Sam (eng-runtime): Confirmed. We should hold off on further precision rollouts to dedicated pools until calibration pipeline is hardened. Action items:
- Devin: add sequence-length cap and memory guard to calibration job (blocking)
- Sam: add runtime fallback config and a canary rule for streaming routes
- Jia: add dashboard alert for calibration job OOMs and a runbook change to auto-rollback precision profiles on specific telemetry patterns
- Ava: coordinate customer comms and status update to support

Devin (ml-infra): Working on cap now. Quick patch to the calib job config: `--max-seq 8192` and a streaming-safe sampling mode. Pushing to infra staging.

Maria (cs): Thanks. I'll post an update to the affected customers: short summary + rollback confirmation + ETA for postmortem.

Jia (eng-sre): Severity set to Sev2 for now (customer impacting but rollback mitigated). Creating incident doc: https://confluence.redwood.example/display/INC/1923456789

Sam (eng-runtime): For post-incident follow-up: we should add unit tests that exercise dequant path on long-but-common sequence patterns and add a canary gate to stop aggressive profiles from reaching streaming pools.

Ava (oncall): Handoff to next oncall (Ava -> Priya) at 1923457900. Summary: p99 spike caused by aggressive precision profile rollout (v3-int8-aggressive). Calibration job produced outlier sequences causing OOM and a bad profile causing expensive dequant path. Rollback completed, p95/p99 recovering. Next steps: infra fix for calib, runtime fallback, smaller canary window for precision rollouts. Owners: Devin (calib fix), Sam (runtime fallback / canary), Jia (observability & runbook), Maria (customer comms).

Ava (oncall): Leaving notes in incident doc and tagging follow-ups. If anyone sees new regressions, ping `#incidents` and page oncall. :warning:

end of thread
